newsitem.title: USA: NIMO Albany environmental management certified.
newsitem.headline: NIMO Albany environmental management certified.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said its the Albany Steam Station has become the first power plant in the Northeast certified to a new international standard for environmental management.

Certification under the voluntary International Standard Organization (ISO) 14001 standard demonstrates that the Albany Steam Station operates under an effective environmental management system, the utility said.

Although the certification cannot guarantee the long-term continued operation of the plant, Vice President of Fossil and Hydro Generation Thomas H. Baron cited several reasons Niagara Mohawk pursued independent certification under the standard.

"Certification could enhance the competitive opportunities of the facility, strengthen operational controls, and reinforce employee understanding of and commitment to environmental objectives," said Baron.

The United States signed the ISO 14001 standard when it was finalized in September 1996. The purpose of the standard is to ensure that companies develop management systems for improving overall environmental performance by reducing pollution and other impacts and improving use of resources.

Fair noted that because Niagara Mohawk has a well-developed corporate environmental management system in place, the company incurred minimal costs in attaining certification and spent no money on capital improvements.

The 400,000-kilowatt plant is located on the Hudson River about three miles south of Albany. The plant began operation in 1952 with coal as its primary fuel. It was converted to burn oil in 1970, and the company added the capability of burning natural gas in 1981.
